prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a new temple was dedicated from 2004 to 2008 (not rededications).
prompts.text_original: A country where a new temple was dedicated from 2004 through 2008 (not counting rededications).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (original dedication dates) and the Church temple list, read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: From 2004 through 2008 new temples reached Africa, Europe and Central America. Africa gained Accra Ghana (2004) and Aba Nigeria (2005), and Europe gained Copenhagen Denmark (2004) and Helsinki Finland (2006). Panama City (2008) was Panama's first temple, and the United States added temples such as Manhattan New York and Rexburg Idaho.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Manhattan New York (2004); San Antonio Texas and Newport Beach California (2005); Sacramento California (2006); Rexburg Idaho and Twin Falls Idaho (2008).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose first temple was dedicated from 1996 to 2009.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country or territory whose first temple was dedicated between 1996 and 2009.
prompts.summary: Between 1996 and 2009 many countries got their first temple, including Hong Kong (1996), Spain (1999), Ghana (2004) and Nigeria (2005). The year 2000 alone brought first temples to Bolivia, Costa Rica, Fiji, Venezuela and the Dominican Republic.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that Saints names on David O. McKay's 1952 European tour.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 3 ch. 36: David O. McKay's six-week European tour in 1952 took in these countries. Pin one.
prompts.summary: In 1952 President David O. McKay made a six-week tour of Europe, visiting Great Britain, the Netherlands, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Switzerland, France and Germany. In Switzerland he chose a site for the first temple in Europe, which was dedicated near Bern in 1955.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Where he chose a site for Europe's first temple.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with 200,000 to 500,000 Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country with between 200,000 and 500,000 Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 six countries had between 200,000 and 500,000 Church members: Guatemala, Ecuador, Nigeria, Bolivia, Colombia and Canada. Nigeria, with about 274,000, had the most Latter-day Saints in Africa.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: About 274,000 members, the most in Africa.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country holding a nation judged in Amos 1-2, Jeremiah 46-51 or Ezekiel 25-29.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a nation judged in the oracles of Amos 1-2, Jeremiah 46-51 or Ezekiel 25-29
prompts.summary: Amos, Jeremiah and Ezekiel each delivered oracles, or prophetic messages, warning the nations around Israel of coming judgment. Egypt, Babylon, Damascus, Tyre, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, Edom and the Philistine cities all received warnings, and Amos did not spare Israel itself (Amos 2:6). Jeremiah gave two long chapters to Babylon's fall (Jeremiah 50-51), and Ezekiel gave three to Tyre and Sidon.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Jeremiah 46 opens with Egypt, and Ezekiel calls Pharaoh a great dragon in the river (Ezekiel 29:3).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Two long chapters foretell Babylon's fall (Jeremiah 50-51).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Amos judges Israel itself, and all three prophets judge Philistine cities now in Israel (Amos 1:8; 2:6; Jeremiah 47:5; Ezekiel 25:15-17).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Ammon, Moab and Edom are judged by all three prophets (Amos 1-2; Jeremiah 48-49; Ezekiel 25).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Tyre is judged for selling captives, and Ezekiel gives three chapters to Tyre and Sidon (Amos 1:9; Ezekiel 26-28).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Amos judges Gaza (Amos 1:6-7), now in the Gaza Strip.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Damascus gets the first oracle in Amos and is told it will grow feeble (Amos 1:3; Jeremiah 49:23-27).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Elam, in south-west Iran, is promised scattering (Jeremiah 49:34-39).
